headline: Green360 Technologies signs first binding commercial supply agreement with Holcim for low-carbon cement replacement product in Victoria
reasoning: Green360 Technologies has signed its first binding commercial offtake agreement with Holcim, one of the global leaders in concrete and cement production, to supply its calcined kaolin-based supplementary cementitious material (SCM) to approximately five batching plants around Melbourne. The initial agreement covers just under 5,000 tonnes from Green360's stage-one commercial capacity of 30,000 tonnes, with plans to sign up other major concrete producers to fill remaining capacity. The company is vertically integrated, owning the ore body and manufacturing facility in Victoria, and already produces around 24,000 tonnes annually for traditional markets such as paints, adhesives and pharmaceuticals. The product addresses both a structural supply cliff in fly ash and slag caused by coal-fired power station closures and the embodied carbon challenge, as cement accounts for up to 10% of global CO2 emissions. CEO Aaron Banks describes the Holcim agreement as commercial validation of both the product's technical capabilities and the company's ability to deliver at commercial scale into major supply chains, with a longer-term ambition to scale into hundreds of thousands of tonnes up and down Australia's eastern seaboard.

So we've, we've ticked the box that this can now come in at scale, which then gives a level of comfortability to the government and the asset owners to start prescribing the material as well.

headline: Green360 Technologies secures landmark commercial contract validating its supplementary cementitious material at scale, with pipeline near fully filled and financials strengthening.
reasoning: Aaron Banks describes the contract as a landmark commercial validation, demonstrating that Green360's product can enter major supply chains and be delivered on-spec at commercial scale quantities without requiring significant changes to customer batching plants. The company has ~$3.5–4 million in the bank as of March, with current sales escalating and a circa 20% price increase now applied across clients. The pipeline for remaining ~25,000 tonnes of existing product is expected to be filled by year-end, alongside the launch of new scaled products including calcined clay targeting the eastern seaboard. A scoping study due at end of year will outline the size of a potential 500,000–600,000 tonne supply opportunity, which Banks believes will materially shift market understanding of the company's scale potential.

headline: Australia faces imminent structural shortage of fly ash and slag driven by coal-fired power station closures, threatening concrete supply chain along the eastern seaboard
reasoning: Fly ash and slag, cheap byproducts of coal-fired power generation, are essential components of modern concrete for durability and cost management; without them, no concrete can be poured. Policy-driven closure of coal-fired power stations is creating a supply cliff that is already beginning to disrupt concrete batching plants along Australia's east coast. Even one additional power station closure is sufficient to start disrupting supply at a material scale. The incumbents' abundance and low cost have historically kept concrete prices contained, but that dynamic is now reversing. This structural gap represents the core market opportunity for Green360's calcined kaolin SCM product, which carries no green premium and offers superior durability characteristics.
